body.statement:
For every \(\theta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}\) and every integer \(k\geq2\),
\[
 m_k-\beta c_k=\alpha^{k-1}\gamma u_k\in A,
 \qquad Q_Am_k=\beta Q_Ac_k.
\]
These identities require only finite moments through order \(k\), source independence, and the population-plane restriction; they do not require a moment generating function.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(\theta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}\) and an integer \(k\geq2\).  All moments appearing below are finite by the all-absolute-moments condition in the definition of \(\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}\).  For random variables \(X_1,\ldots,X_k\) with finite absolute moments through order \(k\), their joint cumulant is the finite moment--cumulant polynomial
\[
 \kappa_k(X_1,\ldots,X_k)
 =\sum_{\pi\in\mathfrak P_k}(|\pi|-1)!(-1)^{|\pi|-1}
   \prod_{D\in\pi}\mathbb E\!\left[\prod_{j\in D}X_j\right],             \tag{1}
\]
where \(\mathfrak P_k\) is the set of partitions of \(\{1,\ldots,k\}\).  Formula (1) is multilinear because, after each product is expanded, every argument occurs exactly once in every summand.  It also shows that a cumulant involving variables from two independent source families is zero.  To verify the latter without an analytic moment-generating function, introduce the finite formal moment series in indeterminates \(t_1,\ldots,t_k\), retain only monomials in which every exponent is at most one, and expand the formal logarithm \(\log(1+z)=\sum_{j=1}^k(-1)^{j-1}z^j/j\).  The coefficient of \(t_1\cdots t_k\) is exactly (1).  Independence factors the formal moment series into one factor for each independent source family, so its formal logarithm is a sum of terms involving only one family; hence every mixed coefficient vanishes.  This argument uses only the finitely many moments in (1).

Define the proof-local treatment-source contrast
\[
 v_k=\bigl(\kappa_k(\epsilon_{t,e})-
                 \kappa_k(\epsilon_{t,0})\bigr)_{e=1}^{E-1}.
\]
The structural equations give
\[
 T_e=\alpha\epsilon_{u,e}+\epsilon_{t,e},
 \qquad
 Y_e=(\alpha\beta+\gamma)\epsilon_{u,e}
       +\beta\epsilon_{t,e}+\epsilon_y.                                  \tag{2}
\]
By multilinearity of (1), mutual independence of the three sources, and vanishing of mixed-source cumulants,
\[
 \kappa_k(T_e)=\alpha^k\kappa_k(\epsilon_{u,e})
                  +\kappa_k(\epsilon_{t,e}),                              \tag{3}
\]
and, because \(k\geq2\),
\[
 \kappa_k(Y_e,T_e,\ldots,T_e)
 =(alpha\beta+\gamma)\alpha^{k-1}\kappa_k(\epsilon_{u,e})
   +\beta\kappa_k(\epsilon_{t,e}).                                       \tag{4}
\]
The invariant outcome source contributes nothing to (4): any term selecting \(\epsilon_y\) in the first argument and a treatment source in a remaining argument is a mixed cumulant of independent families.

Subtracting the baseline-environment versions of (3)--(4) and using the definitions of \(u_k,c_k,m_k\) yields
\[
 c_k=\alpha^ku_k+v_k,                                                       \tag{5}
\]
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 m_k
 &=(\alpha\beta+\gamma)\alpha^{k-1}u_k+\beta v_k\\
 &=\beta(\alpha^ku_k+v_k)+\alpha^{k-1}\gamma u_k
  =\beta c_k+\alpha^{k-1}\gamma u_k.                                     \tag{6}
 \end{aligned}
\]
The population-plane restriction gives \(u_k\in A\), so (6) proves \(m_k-\beta c_k\in A\).  Since \(\operatorname{rank}(C)=d\), the matrix \(C^\top C\) is invertible and the declared operator \(Q_A\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(A^\perp\).  Applying it to (6) gives \(Q_Am_k=\beta Q_Ac_k\), as required.
